subject.title: fix(agents): skip error classification for clean non-zero exits

question: Should normally exited non-zero exec results continue warning when the agent produces no user-facing reply, or should OpenClaw introduce an explicit accepted-exit signal for selected command outcomes?
rationale: The runtime cannot infer from exit code and normal process termination alone whether code 1 means an accepted result such as grep no-match or a genuine command failure, while recent merged behavior intentionally preserves no-reply warnings.

options.title: Model accepted exits explicitly
options.body: Preserve generic no-reply failure warnings and redesign the fix so only a typed, owner-provided accepted outcome bypasses classification.

options.title: Keep current behavior
options.body: Close or withdraw this PR and continue relying on successful user-facing replies to suppress recovered exec warnings.

options.title: Suppress all completed exits
options.body: Accept that normally exited non-zero commands may fail silently whenever the agent produces no reply.

recommendation.title: Model accepted exits explicitly
recommendation.body: Preserve generic no-reply failure warnings and redesign the fix so only a typed, owner-provided accepted outcome bypasses classification.

likelyOwner.reason: This person most recently authored and merged the explicit recovered-versus-no-reply exec warning contract.
